name: Structural steel S355J2, the lattice of the Rotunda's eye
summary: A weldable carbon-manganese structural steel of 355 MPa yield, tough at -20 degC (EN 10025-2 S355J2 for plate and flats; EN 10210-1 S355J2H for hot-finished hollow sections). It is the steel of the Rotunda's glazed eye, a triangulated lattice after the British Museum's Great Court roof, whose engineers chose the equivalent British grade (BS 4360 grade 50D) for toughness at the welds. The steel is never seen bare: it is always under its shop-applied paint system (the working 'painted.steel'). It is declared an accent of the glass family because it exists only to carry the glass.

precedent.text: The Great Court roof (Foster and Partners with Buro Happold, fabricated and erected by Waagner-Biro, opened 2000) is a lattice of welded, tapering steel box sections. Buro Happold specified 'Grade D' steel, rather than a lower grade, to reduce the risk of brittle failure at the welds. The members deepen from about 3 in at the Reading Room to about 7 in at the corners.

formation.how: Iron ore is reduced to iron in a blast furnace (or scrap is melted in an electric arc furnace), refined to steel with its carbon and manganese set, cast continuously into slabs or blooms, and hot rolled to plate, flats and sections, or formed and welded into hollow sections. For the lattice the members are cut, bevelled and welded at the nodes in the fabricator's shop, the welds ground and faired.

optics.note: Bare steel is never seen in the museum: the lattice is always under its paint system, whose optics are in the working 'painted.steel'. The bare metal's constants are recorded for cut edges and for checks. They are those of pure iron; a carbon steel's differ little in the visible.

f0.derivation: Unpolarised Fresnel reflectance at normal incidence, R = ((n-1)^2 + k^2) / ((n+1)^2 + k^2), from the tabulated n,k interpolated linearly to 380-780 nm in 10 nm steps (end values held), integrated against the CIE 1931 2-degree colour-matching functions under CIE illuminant D65, normalised so that a perfect reflector has Y = 1, and converted from XYZ to linear Rec.709 with the sRGB matrix.

f82.derivation: As f0, but the unpolarised Fresnel reflectance of the complex index at 82 degrees incidence (the edge tint of N. Hoffman's F82 model).

acoustic.note: The lattice's members are slender and lie under the glazing; they are not an acoustic surface of the Rotunda. No absorption is recorded.

sections.text: Hot-finished rectangular hollow sections (EN 10210-2 dimensions) in S355J2H, or plates and flats in S355J2 welded into boxes where members taper, as in the Great Court.
sections.source: EN 10210-1/-2 (hot-finished structural hollow sections); Great Court precedent: S. Hart, Architectural Record (January 2003), via Cantilever, https://cantilever.wordpress.com/about-innovation/buro-happold-british-museum/

asBuiltMembers.text: The as-built eye: a ring (r 2.42-2.50 m) carrying the glass at 20.38 m, bars in three directions 60 degrees apart and 0.8 m apart, each bar 0.05 m wide and 0.10 m deep (half-extents 0.025 m and 0.05 m).

uses.where: the lattice of the Rotunda's glazed eye (D-004)
uses.source: MuseeVision/Journal/Decisions.md, D-004 (the steel-and-glass lattice eye stays as built, after the British Museum's Great Court)

photograph: The lattice reads as slender dark grey bars against the sky, with a soft satin sheen.
The paint's faint orange-peel texture shows only close to; welded nodes are faired smooth, with no bolts and no rust bleed.
Seen from below at a low angle, the upper edges of the bars carry a slightly lighter film of dust.

familyDeclaration.text: D-014 admits the families stone, white, bronze, oak, accent, glass, water and living, and an accent names the core family it ties back to. Painted structural steel belongs to none of the core families; in the museum it appears only as the structure of glazing, so it is declared an accent of the glass family. The Architect may overturn this reading with a new decision.
familyDeclaration.source: MuseeVision/Journal/Decisions.md, D-014 (Matter); D-004 (the Rotunda's eye is glazed)

unverified.reason: Architectural Record says only 'Grade D steel'. Reading it as grade 50D (and so S355J2) assumes the common 355 MPa strength class; 43D (S275J2) would also be 'Grade D'. Brown and Cook (2002) was not readable (HTTP 403).
